plane_or_setting: Cross-setting; no single official faction, plane, guild, college, or civilization

core_identity.short_form: All five colors are available. What brings them together depends on the deck.
core_identity.summary: Five-Color / WUBRG gives a Commander deck access to White, Blue, Black, Red, and Green. That access does not establish one universal philosophy, motive, role, or play pattern.
core_identity.philosophy: Five-Color is philosophically plural. A commander, tribe, mechanic, theme, toolbox, or other deck plan determines why all five colors are present; integration, coalition, and synthesis are possible Vox Mana readings rather than identity-wide doctrine.
core_identity.central_tension: Broader color access increases mana requirements and consistency pressure, while the reason for using that access remains deck-specific.
core_identity.identity_frame: Use Five-Color as public-facing language and WUBRG as technical metadata. Keep all lore, Commander, and deck claims source-bound.

semantic_model.identity_floor: Five-Color means access to White, Blue, Black, Red, and Green at the Commander deck-construction layer; it does not supply one universal motive, role, metaphysics, or play pattern.
semantic_model.hero_anchor: All five colors are available. What brings them together depends on the deck.
semantic_model.vox_mana_lens: Integration, coalition, and synthesis are optional Vox Mana interpretations. Full-Spectrum Integrator is one exploration archetype, not the definition of Five-Color.

exploration_archetypes.name: Full-Spectrum Integrator
exploration_archetypes.description: Coordinates distinct color contributions or requirements into one coherent plan; this lens fits some Five-Color decks, not the identity as a whole.

exploration_archetypes.name: Five-Color Toolbox
exploration_archetypes.description: Uses broad color access to assemble answers or effects selected by a particular commander or plan.

exploration_archetypes.name: Five-Color Typal
exploration_archetypes.description: Uses all five colors because a creature type, commander, or typal payoff spans the color pie.

exploration_archetypes.name: Rainbow Payoffs
exploration_archetypes.description: Uses cards that reward assembling, spending, controlling, or representing several or all five colors.

great_tension.gift: All five colors are available for the commander, tribe, mechanic, theme, toolbox, or payoff that calls for them.
great_tension.shadow: Broad access can strain consistency or become unfocused accumulation when the deck has no clear reason for using it.
great_tension.boundary: Any integration, coalition, or synthesis language is an optional Vox Mana archetype or interpretive lens, not official Wizards canon or universal Five-Color doctrine.

mechanics.summary: Literal five-color identity and all-five requirements are defining signals; WUBRG costs or activations are strong signals; sunburst and converge are strongly associated; Domain and basic-land-type checks are compatible but nonexclusive; color-count, multicolor, gold, and typal themes are situational; fixing is infrastructure, while ramp is only supportive. Specific cards remain manual-verify support until exact sources are captured.

pair_overlap_boundaries: A single color's priority alone is not Five-Color.
A guild or college overlap is not Five-Color unless all five colors remain present and meaningful.
Commander support links do not turn deck preference into placement evidence.
near_match_boundaries: Colorless is outside-WUBRG restriction, not WUBRG totality.
Four-color identities are missing-color frames; WUBRG has no missing color.
Five-color Eldrazi support is not Colorless proof.
Generic goodstuff is not a universal Five-Color meaning; it is one possible deck-construction outcome rather than identity proof.
Mana fixing alone is not Five-Color identity.
A WUBRG commander row is support-only unless the identity claim is separately sourced.

research_limitations: Do not use local WUBRG essays as raw-claim evidence unless their individual claims are mapped to captured sources.
Do not use generated/runtime JSON, dossier output, or placement output as lore evidence.
Do not use Commander support rows as placement proof, lore proof, legality proof, or recommendation-quality proof.
Do not use product anchors as color philosophy, metaphysics, lore proof, or representative Five-Color play-pattern proof.
Do not use WUBRG as a public Home preview or route expansion.
Do not treat WUBRG as a universal superset, best identity, endpoint identity, completion state, or default high-complexity answer.
Do not pad WUBRG with weak claims to match other identities.

profile.overview: Five-Color / WUBRG is access to White, Blue, Black, Red, and Green. The commander, tribe, mechanic, theme, toolbox, or other deck plan supplies the reason for combining them.
profile.philosophy: Five-Color has no single identity-wide philosophy. Vox Mana may explore integration, coalition, or synthesis as optional readings, but those readings do not define every Five-Color deck.
profile.core_tension: Broader color access increases mana requirements and consistency pressure, while purpose and play pattern remain deck-specific.
profile.mechanics_and_play_pattern: Literal all-five requirements and WUBRG costs or activations are direct signals; sunburst and converge are strongly associated; Domain and basic-land-type checks are compatible but nonexclusive; other multicolor, color-count, typal, fixing, and ramp patterns require qualification.
